Here is a comprehensive, up-to-date overview of UK bridging loan statistics as of mid-2026, structured by key metrics and supported by multiple reliable sources:

---

##  1. Market Size and Loan Book

- **Total Loan Book**  
  The Bridging & Development Lenders Association (BDLA) reports that as of Q1 2026, the total outstanding bridging and development loan book stood at approximately £11.5 billion, following a peak of around £13.4 billion in Q4 2025. ([theintermediary.co.uk](https://theintermediary.co.uk/2026/03/bridging-loan-applications-rise-to-11-7bn-as-sector-holds-firm-bdla/?utm_source=openai))

- **Market Growth Projection**  
  Forecasts indicate that the overall UK bridging finance market is expected to reach roughly £12.2 billion in outstanding loans by the end of 2026. ([lendingbridge.co.uk](https://www.lendingbridge.co.uk/blogs/uk-bridging-loans-market-growth2026?utm_source=openai))

- **Historical Growth Trajectory**  
  A snapshot of annual gross lending shows substantial growth: from approximately £4.94 bn in 2022, to £5.76 bn in 2023 (up ~16%), to £7.34 bn in 2024 (up ~27%), and then exceeding £13 bn in 2025. The total loan book is projected to surpass £12 bn in 2026. ([fundingagent.co.uk](https://www.fundingagent.co.uk/post/bridging-finance-statistics-uk?utm_source=openai))

- **Scale Expansion**  
  In May 2026, BDLA data highlighted that the bridging market had doubled in size over the previous five years and that their panel of specialist lenders—over 100 members—was tracking a combined loan book of around £13 bn. ([bridging.fund](https://www.bridging.fund/market-updates/uk-bridging-market-scale-pricing-may-2026/?utm_source=openai))

---

##  2. Applications and Completions

- **Applications**  
  - Q4 2025: £11.7 bn in applications, up 2.6% from the prior quarter. ([theintermediary.co.uk](https://theintermediary.co.uk/2026/03/bridging-loan-applications-rise-to-11-7bn-as-sector-holds-firm-bdla/?utm_source=openai))  
  - Q1 2026: Applications moderated to £9.9 bn, reflecting a more measured market environment. ([cherryplc.co.uk](https://www.cherryplc.co.uk/industry/pressreleases/details/23809?utm_source=openai))

- **Completions**  
  - Q4 2025: Completed lending totaled just under £2.5 bn. ([theintermediary.co.uk](https://theintermediary.co.uk/2026/03/bridging-loan-applications-rise-to-11-7bn-as-sector-holds-firm-bdla/?utm_source=openai))  
  - Q1 2026: Completions fell to £1.8 bn. ([cherryplc.co.uk](https://www.cherryplc.co.uk/industry/pressreleases/details/23809?utm_source=openai))

---

##  3. Interest Rates, Terms, and LTV

- **Interest Rates**  
  - Q3 2025: Average monthly interest rate was around 0.85%, up from 0.81% in Q2. ([mortgagesolutions.co.uk](https://www.mortgagesolutions.co.uk/specialist-lending/bridging/2025/11/13/bridging-lending-hits-209-4m-in-q3/?utm_source=openai))  
  - Q1 2026: Average monthly rate slightly eased to 0.82%. ([mpamag.com](https://www.mpamag.com/uk/mortgage-types/bridging/bridging-lending-holds-steady-in-q1/575140?utm_source=openai))  
  - May 2026 market floor rates varied by LTV and purpose: for first-charge residential at sub-55% LTV, rates ranged from 0.85%–0.95% per month; higher LTVs and complex deals carried higher rates up to 1.75%. ([bridging.fund](https://www.bridging.fund/market-updates/uk-bridging-market-scale-pricing-may-2026/?utm_source=openai))

- **Loan-to-Value (LTV)**  
  - Q3 2025: Average LTV stood at approximately 55%. ([mortgagesolutions.co.uk](https://www.mortgagesolutions.co.uk/specialist-lending/bridging/2025/11/13/bridging-lending-hits-209-4m-in-q3/?utm_source=openai))  
  - Q1 2026: Average LTV reduced to around 52–56.6%, suggesting a conservative lending approach. ([cherryplc.co.uk](https://www.cherryplc.co.uk/industry/pressreleases/details/23809?utm_source=openai))

- **Loan Terms & Completion Times**  
  - Q3 2025: Average term was 12 months; average completion time was 41 days (down from 48 days in Q2). ([mortgagesolutions.co.uk](https://www.mortgagesolutions.co.uk/specialist-lending/bridging/2025/11/13/bridging-lending-hits-209-4m-in-q3/?utm_source=openai))  
  - Q1 2026: Completion time averaged 53 days; term remained around 12 months. ([mpamag.com](https://www.mpamag.com/uk/mortgage-types/bridging/bridging-lending-holds-steady-in-q1/575140?utm_source=openai))  
  - Q2 2026: Forbes Advisor reported Q1 2026 bridging loan volume at ~£200 m, with average completion time of 53 days and term of 12 months. ([forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/uk/loans/best-bridging-loans/?utm_source=openai))

---

##  4. Purpose and Loan Types

- **Common Uses**  
  - Q1 2026: Investment purchase remained the most common purpose at 22% of all bridging transactions—unchanged from Q4 2025. ([mpamag.com](https://www.mpamag.com/uk/mortgage-types/bridging/bridging-lending-holds-steady-in-q1/575140?utm_source=openai))

- **Regulated vs. Unregulated**  
  - Unregulated bridging loans rose to 59% of the market in Q1 2026, the highest level since Q4 2021 (64%). ([mpamag.com](https://www.mpamag.com/uk/mortgage-types/bridging/bridging-lending-holds-steady-in-q1/575140?utm_source=openai))

- **Security Positions**  
  - Q3 2025: Around 88% of bridging deals were first-charge; 12% were second-charge. ([mortgagesolutions.co.uk](https://www.mortgagesolutions.co.uk/specialist-lending/bridging/2025/11/13/bridging-lending-hits-209-4m-in-q3/?utm_source=openai))

---

##  5. Market Dynamics & Sentiment

- **Governance and Consolidation**  
  The 2026 Interpath & BDLA Bridging Market Survey indicates increasing governance and consolidation in the sector. Macroeconomic uncertainty was cited as a top concern by 65% of respondents (up from 39% in 2025). There is growing focus on independent verification of security and robust underwriting. ([interpath.com](https://interpath.com/media-hub/articles/increased-governance-and-more-consolidation-to-shape-bridging-finance-market-interpath-bdla-bridging-market-survey-2026/?utm_source=openai))

- **Development Finance Appetite**  
  Around half of market participants reported increasing selective exposure to development finance, signaling optimism in this segment. ([interpath.com](https://interpath.com/media-hub/articles/increased-governance-and-more-consolidation-to-shape-bridging-finance-market-interpath-bdla-bridging-market-survey-2026/?utm_source=openai))

- **Market Competitiveness**  
  By mid-2026, the sector had broadened significantly, with over 100 specialist lenders. Pricing became more competitive due to increased capital, improved underwriting infrastructure, and institutional recognition of bridging as an asset class. ([bridging.fund](https://www.bridging.fund/market-updates/uk-bridging-market-scale-pricing-may-2026/?utm_source=openai))

---

##  Summary Table

 Metric | Value / Trend
---|---
Total Loan Book | £11.5 bn (Q1 2026), forecast to reach £12.2 bn by end of 2026
Applications | £11.7 bn (Q4 2025) → £9.9 bn (Q1 2026)
Completions | £2.5 bn (Q4 2025) → £1.8 bn (Q1 2026)
Interest Rate (monthly) | ~0.85% (Q3 2025), ~0.82% (Q1 2026), market floor 0.85–0.95% for low LTV
Average LTV | ~55% (Q3 2025), ~52–56.6% (Q1 2026)
Loan Term | ~12 months
Completion Time | 41 days (Q3 2025), 53 days (Q1 2026)
Use | 22% investment purchase
Regulation | 59% unregulated (Q1 2026)
Market Sentiment | Cautiously optimistic; stronger governance and selective development finance growth

---

##  Final Thoughts

The UK bridging loan market has expanded significantly in recent years, now boasting a loan book exceeding £11 billion and poised to surpass £12 billion by end of 2026. Despite a slight softening in activity early in the year, overall demand remains strong. Borrowers benefit from improved pricing, faster completion times, and a broader choice of lenders. Lenders, meanwhile, are adopting more rigorous governance and increasingly focusing on development finance. This maturity signals a sector evolving from niche to mainstream within UK property finance.
